# Decisions: speed-2

- 2026-08-03T10:22:33.462Z — chose **Split the CLI into a 545-byte dist/cli.js stub + 76KB dist/fast.js (hooks, statusline) + 986KB dist/full.js, with the stub calling module.enableCompileCache() before either import. fast.ts owns only the exact argv shapes the shims emit and returns false for anything else, falling through to the full CLI.** over Lazy dynamic imports inside the existing single bundle (esbuild inlines them back, so nothing is saved), or a second hand-written hook implementation (two sources of truth for hook behavior). because Measured: hooks were compiling 986KB (MCP SDK, chokidar, commander, cloud, doctor) to append one line. Hot path 56-64ms to 26-28ms; the slow path also improved 60ms to 47ms because the stub makes the compile cache actually apply. Falling through on unrecognized shapes keeps commander the single owner of the command surface, so --help, --version and every error message are byte-identical.
- 2026-08-03T10:32:57.763Z — chose **Skip projection writes whose bytes already match disk (read + compare before writeFileAtomic), leaving the render unconditional.** over Regenerating only the session file the append touched (true O(1)), or caching rendered output in memory across appends. because Measured on a 25-session initiative: rendering every session costs 0.03ms, writing every session costs 3.2ms — the render is 100x cheaper than the write, so caching renders optimizes the wrong half. Targeted regeneration would need to infer which session files an event can change, but renderSession takes the whole InitiativeState, so that inference is unsound. Content-compare is provably output-identical — the file holds the same bytes either way — so no reader can observe it, and it needs no knowledge of which event touched what.
